catalogMeta.label: Build a Paragraph (open build)
catalogMeta.description: Open build, on the live tutor: tap sentence cards into a paragraph in order: the topic sentence first, two or more facts that belong (any order), the closing last, leaving out the two facts about a different topic. Many paragraphs pass. Checked in code from the cards' roles. Organization only; the writing modes judge no sentence. Beta = informational + 0.1.

cards.text: Sea turtles are large reptiles that swim in oceans.
They have hard shells on their backs.
They use flippers to paddle in the water.
Mother turtles lay eggs on sandy beaches.
They hold their breath while diving deep.
Jellyfish float along ocean currents.
Sharks have sharp teeth in their jaws.
Now you know all about sea turtles.
Dolphins are smart mammals that live in the sea.
They breathe air through a blowhole.
They swim together in groups called pods.
They use clicks and whistles to talk.
They leap high out of the water.
Crabs walk sideways along the ocean floor.
Eels hide inside dark rocky caves.
These facts show how amazing dolphins are.
Octopuses are clever sea animals without any bones.
They have eight flexible arms with suckers.
They squirt dark ink to escape danger.
They can change their skin color quickly.
They have three hearts inside their bodies.
Whales sing loud songs across the ocean.
Starfish have tiny tube feet for walking.
That is why octopuses are so special.
